newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks stretch gains on Fed cheer.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks stretch gains on Fed cheer.

text.p: Argentine stocks pushed higher at the close Tuesday, spurred on by the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged, dealers said.
"The Fed's lack of action on rates was an incentive to build up positions taken in recent weeks, and this mild-mannered advance should continue," said Jose Napoli at brokers Ignoto y Napoli.
The blue-chip MerVal index recorded its seventh consecutive gain, rising 1.3 percent to a three-month high of 754.07.

"The market has finally pierced resistance at 750 and will now aim to set a new high for 1997, although without euphoria because it's slightly overbought," another trader said, noting bellwether YPF closed Tuesday at a record price of $29.2 per share.
So far this year the MerVal peaked on February 24 at 759.72, its highest level in nearly five years.

Bolsa turnover picked up after the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee wound up its monthly meeting Tuesday without raising interest rates. Activity had ground to token levels Monday ahead of the FOMC talks.
Floor volume totalled 19.5 million pesos against 12.7 million Monday, while over-the-counter deals amounted to 67.7 million pesos against 65.3 million Monday.
The broad market matched MerVal gains of 1.3 percent, with risers beating decliners 35 to 12 and 24 issues closing flat.
During the session a stock exchange seat was sold by brokers Rio Valores to brokers Aldazabal y Cia for 500,000 pesos, the same price fetched at the previous auction April 2.
Top main-tier gainers were oil company Astra, carmaker Sevel and construction stock Polledo, which rallied 4.3 percent, 3.0 percent and 2.9 percent, respectively.
Losers were led by steelmaker Siderar, electricity generator Central Puerto and foods giant Molinos, which added 1.6 percent, 0.7 percent and 0.5 percent, respectively.
